requirement:
The tracked source-read operation resolves the selected `OutlineId` through
the application's source-node mapping and reads that node through `Domain`.
Successful reads delivered to the caller record that node's identity and the
fingerprint of its supplied contents.

The graph's recording and freshness contracts apply under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.provider_observations`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request implementation source.

**Obligation 1: resolve the `OutlineId` through the application's source-node mapping and read that node through `Domain`.**
- `direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs`) calls `read_source` with two unmapped ids: an unknown path, and a known path with an unknown selector. Both return an "unsupported source item" error. The test also asserts the domain saw zero reads, so a failed mapping never reaches `Domain`.
- The same test reads a mapped id and checks `read_nodes == ["source-node", "source-node"]`. This shows the mapped node id, not the path, is what reaches `Domain`.
- `fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies` (same file) reads `source.txt` through the `read_source` tool. The output contains "prepared domain contents" and not the on-disk "disk text", so the read goes through `Domain`. It also asserts `read_nodes == ["source-node"]`. Four bad requests (ignored file, `../` escape, unknown selector, malformed selector) all error, and the read count stays at 1.
- `supplied_agent_uses_attached_project_tools_in_both_configuration_orders` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs`) runs an agent with attached sources in both configuration orders. The mapped read returns the domain snapshot, not the disk contents, and the domain records exactly the one selected `OutlineId`.
- `source_capable_validator_tracks_deterministic_reads_and_reuses_saved_results` covers the validator path in both attachment orders, and the domain's changed text is reflected in the output.

**Obligation 2: successful delivered reads record the node identity and the fingerprint of the supplied contents.**
- In `direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns`, the dependencies equal `[Node("source-node", returned.fingerprint())]`. The record's `is_current` check then holds before the domain text changes and fails after it.
- The fixed-tools test asserts `read.dependencies` equals `Node("source-node", Content("prepared domain contents").fingerprint())`. This is an independently computed fingerprint of the supplied contents.
- The same test checks that every `get_next_page` continuation carries the same dependencies. This holds even after the domain text is changed to "replacement", so the recorded observation is of what was actually delivered.
- `cached_selected_source_reads_record_exact_delivered_contents_and_errors_add_no_input` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs`) checks the recorded fingerprint value equals the selected node's delivered text exactly. A failing read of `fn[missing]` adds no observation.
- `source_tools_keep_search_discovery_separate_from_delivered_source_reads` checks that only the delivered read is recorded, as `Node(7)` with the provider-supplied snapshot, and not the earlier search. `source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads` checks that list, search and outline calls and their pages register no observation.

**Failure cases.**
- The mapping error and the domain-read error both leave `inspection.dependencies()` empty. This is in the direct-read test, with `fail_read` toggled.
- Tests of the cited `node_inputs` and `checking_records` contracts are not required here. Their obligations are assessed under those requirements.

No untested obligation or weak assertion remains. Each test is marked with a `{test}` reference to the subject.

Successful reads delivered to the caller record that node's identity and the
fingerprint of its supplied contents.
The graph's recording and freshness contracts apply under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
:::{req} node_inputs
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
// Method on Validator<D>.
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<O>(
&self,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The method observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
